```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, dpi = 96)
library(covassistedGM)
```

## The data

Section 5 of Niu et al. (2024) analyses 883 TCGA breast tumours. The graphical data $Y$ are
reverse-phase protein array measurements of 15 proteins, twelve on the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis
and the three hormone and growth factor receptors; the covariates $X$ are the mRNA expression
of the three receptor genes, whose status defines the clinical subtypes of breast cancer. The
question is whether the protein network differs between tumour groups induced by receptor
expression, without fixing those groups in advance. Both matrices are standardised.

```{r data}
data(brca_rna); data(brca_rppa)
dim(brca_rna); dim(brca_rppa)
colnames(brca_rppa)
round(cor(brca_rna), 2)
```

## Fitting the PxG model

The call below is the authors' `RealDataAnalysis.R` verbatim, apart from the data object
names and `verbose = FALSE`. The authors' samplers keep an $n \times n \times n_{mcmc}$
co-clustering array in memory for Dahl's partition estimate; with the paper's chain (1,000
burn-in and 10,000 kept iterations) on 883 tumours that is 62 GB, so the package ships two
things instead of running it here: the authors' own saved results from that chain
(`inst/original_supplement/RData`), and the results of `reproduce/run_breast_cancer.R`, which
runs the unchanged samplers on all 883 tumours with a shorter chain (200 burn-in, 1,000 kept,
6 GB). The code is the authors'; only `burnin` and `nmcmc` differ. On a machine with enough
memory, `PXG_FULL=TRUE Rscript reproduce/run_breast_cancer.R` runs the paper's chain.

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
p <- 3; q <- 15; n <- 883
set.seed(2022)
A <- PxG_PL(YData = brca_rppa, XData = brca_rna,
            spike = 0.01, slab = 1, a1 = 1, a2 = 1, alphaG = 0.5,
            mu0 = rep(0, p), sigsq0 = 1, b1 = 30, b2 = 0.1,
            M = 10, N = 4, burnin = 1000, nmcmc = 10000, z0 = sample(1:4, n, TRUE), B = 1,
            verbose = FALSE)
set.seed(2022)
C <- GraphOnly_PL(YData = brca_rppa, XData = brca_rna,
                  spike = 0.01, slab = 1, a1 = 1, a2 = 1, alphaG = 0.5,
                  mu0 = rep(0, p), sigsq0 = 1, b1 = 30, b2 = 0.1,
                  M = 10, N = 4, burnin = 1000, nmcmc = 10000, z0 = sample(1:4, n, TRUE), B = 1,
                  verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r load-results}
res <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "brca_pxg_results.rds", package = "covassistedGM"))
str(res$settings)
```

The priors deserve a comment. `spike = 0.01` and `slab = 1` put the neighbourhood-regression
coefficients either close to zero or on the scale of the standardised data; `alphaG = 0.5`
is an uninformative edge prior; `b1 = 30, b2 = 0.1` is a tight inverse-gamma prior on the
covariate variance, which with `M = 10` and `N = 4` lets the three receptor genes drive a
partition into at most four groups.

## Posterior clustering (paper Figure 10)

The authors' chain gives the partition and DIC values reported in the paper (37,531 for PxG
and 40,798 for the graph-only model):

```{r labels-authors}
table(PxG_authors = res$authors$pxg_Label)
table(graph_only_authors = res$authors$graph_only_Label)
c(DIC_PxG = res$authors$pxg_DIC, DIC_graph_only = res$authors$graph_only_DIC)
```

The package's shorter chain, same code and seed, gives:

```{r labels}
table(PxG_package = res$pxg$Label)
table(graph_only_package = res$graph_only$Label)
c(DIC_PxG = res$pxg$DIC, DIC_graph_only = res$graph_only$DIC)
```

DIC values from chains of different lengths are not comparable (the variance term depends on
the number of draws), but the partitions can be compared directly. The cross-table of the two
PxG partitions, and the share of tumours placed in the same group under the best matching of
labels:

```{r compare-authors}
table(package = res$pxg$Label, authors = res$authors$pxg_Label)
res$agreement
```

Plotting the clusters against pairs of receptor genes reproduces Figure 10: the four groups
line up with HER2-high, ER/PR-high, and ER/PR-low tumours. First the authors' partition, then
the package run.

```{r fig10, fig.height = 3.2, fig.width = 9}
cols <- c("#1170AA", "#EF6F6A", "#009E73", "#000000"); pchs <- c(16, 17, 15, 18)
lab <- res$authors$pxg_Label
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2, 1))
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "ESR1"], col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "ESR1 (ER)", main = "authors' chain")
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
plot(brca_rna[, "ESR1"],  brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ESR1 (ER)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
legend("bottomright", paste("Cluster", 1:4), col = cols, pch = pchs, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

```{r fig10-package, fig.height = 3.2, fig.width = 9}
lab <- res$pxg$Label
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2, 1))
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2, 1))
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "ESR1"], col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "ESR1 (ER)", main = "package run")
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
plot(brca_rna[, "ESR1"],  brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ESR1 (ER)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
```

The graph-only partition ignores the receptors and is correspondingly less homogeneous in
covariate space (paper Figure 11). The paper measures this with a within-cluster sum of
squares of the covariates and reports 509,029 for PxG against 645,585 for graph-only. The
script's expression that produces those numbers accumulates each cluster's sum of squares
once per member and recycles the mean vector against the data matrix (see
`?within_cluster_ss`), so `within_cluster_ss()` returns the plain within-cluster sum of
squares, the size-weighted sum, and the script's own value, which matches the two reported
numbers for the authors' partitions:

```{r ss}
pick <- c("ss", "weighted_ss", "script_value")
round(rbind(PxG_authors = unlist(res$ss$pxg_authors[pick]),
            graph_only_authors = unlist(res$ss$graph_only_authors[pick]),
            PxG_package = unlist(res$ss$pxg[pick]),
            graph_only_package = unlist(res$ss$graph_only[pick])), 1)
```

All three versions rank the partitions the same way.

```{r fig11, fig.height = 3.2, fig.width = 9}
lab <- res$authors$graph_only_Label
par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 2, 1))
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "ESR1"], col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "ESR1 (ER)", main = "graph-only model")
plot(brca_rna[, "ERBB2"], brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ERBB2 (HER2)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
plot(brca_rna[, "ESR1"],  brca_rna[, "PGR"],  col = cols[lab], pch = pchs[lab], cex = 0.7, xlab = "ESR1 (ER)", ylab = "PGR (PR)")
```

## One network per cluster (paper Figure 12)

The authors estimate each cluster's graph by rerunning the single-graph neighbourhood
selection sampler `Graph_NS` on that cluster's tumours (`spike = 0.1`, `slab = 5`,
`alphaG = 0.5`, 100 burn-in and 1,000 kept iterations, `set.seed(2022)` before each call),
symmetrising the directed selection frequencies with the maximum rule and declaring an edge
at posterior probability 0.5. `cluster_graphs()` does exactly this. Applied to the authors'
partition it reproduces their saved `probG1`-`probG4` matrices to machine precision (the
refit uses the same code and seed), which is checked in `reproduce/run_breast_cancer.R`:

```{r refit-check}
res$refit_matches_authors
```

The call takes about half a minute for the four clusters, so the saved result is used here.

```{r cluster-graphs, eval = FALSE}
graphs <- cluster_graphs(brca_rppa, res$authors$pxg_Label, spike = 0.1, slab = 5, a1 = 1, a2 = 1,
                         alphaG = 0.5, burnin = 100, nmcmc = 1000, cutoff = 0.5, seed = 2022)
```

```{r graphs-loaded}
graphs <- res$cluster_graphs_authors_labels
sapply(graphs, function(g) c(n = g$n, edges = sum(g$adj) / 2))
```

The heat maps are the package's base-graphics version of Figure 12 (grey scale is the
posterior edge probability, dots mark edges above 0.5):

```{r fig12, fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
for (k in seq_along(graphs)) plot_edge_heatmap(graphs[[k]]$prob, cutoff = 0.5, main = names(graphs)[k])
```

And the same graphs drawn as networks with `Network_VisualizationSB()`: a circular layout,
arcs whose width is the posterior edge probability, and node size equal to the summed
probability of the edges at that protein (its "connectivity degree"). Proteins without a
selected edge are not drawn, which is itself informative.

```{r networks, fig.height = 6.5, fig.width = 6}
plots <- plot_pxg_networks(graphs, title = "PxG cluster networks, TCGA breast cancer", thres = 0.5)
plots[["Cluster 1"]]
plots[["Cluster 2"]]
plots[["Cluster 3"]]
plots[["Cluster 4"]]
```

`pxg_network_matrix()` builds the weight matrix that the plotting function expects (selected
edges carry their posterior probability, everything else is 0), and the function's own output
lets you check that what is drawn is what was selected:

```{r network-check}
M <- pxg_network_matrix(graphs[["Cluster 1"]]$prob, graphs[["Cluster 1"]]$adj)
r <- Network_VisualizationSB(M, NULL, thres = 0.5, regionname = "Cluster 1")
d <- igraph::as_data_frame(r$graph, "edges")
head(d[order(-d$Correlation), ])
c(edges_selected = sum(graphs[["Cluster 1"]]$adj) / 2, edges_drawn = nrow(d))
```

A base-graphics alternative without ggraph is `plot_cluster_network()`:

```{r networks-base, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 4}
plot_cluster_network(graphs[["Cluster 1"]]$prob, graphs[["Cluster 1"]]$adj, main = "Cluster 1 (igraph)")
```

Edges shared by all four clusters and edges private to one cluster are easy to list from the
adjacency matrices:

```{r shared-edges}
adj <- lapply(graphs, `[[`, "adj")
shared <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(adj, function(A) A == 1))
edge_list <- function(M) { idx <- which(M & upper.tri(M), arr.ind = TRUE)
  paste(rownames(M)[idx[, 1]], colnames(M)[idx[, 2]], sep = " - ") }
edge_list(shared)
for (k in seq_along(adj)) {
  others <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(adj[-k], function(A) A == 1))
  cat(names(adj)[k], "only:", paste(edge_list(adj[[k]] == 1 & !others), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

The same graphs for the package's reduced-chain partition are in
`res$cluster_graphs`; the cluster that the two partitions agree on most closely has nearly the
same network:

```{r compare-graphs}
g_pkg <- res$cluster_graphs
sapply(g_pkg, function(g) c(n = g$n, edges = sum(g$adj) / 2))
# correlation of posterior edge probabilities between each package cluster and each authors' cluster
round(outer(seq_along(g_pkg), seq_along(graphs), Vectorize(function(i, k)
  cor(g_pkg[[i]]$prob[upper.tri(g_pkg[[i]]$prob)], graphs[[k]]$prob[upper.tri(graphs[[k]]$prob)]))), 2)
```

## Using the MCMC output directly

`PxG_PL` also returns `Gsum`, the per-sample counts of neighbourhood indicators over the
kept iterations, so one can average edge probabilities over the samples of each cluster
without a refit. This is what `cluster_edge_probabilities()` computes; it was saved too:

```{r gsum}
P <- res$gsum_edge_probabilities
round(P[["Cluster 1"]][1:6, 1:6], 2)
```

These MCMC-averaged probabilities are more conservative than the `Graph_NS` refit because
they integrate over the uncertainty in the partition during the chain, and because the
partition sampler uses `spike = 0.01` and `slab = 1` where the refit uses `0.1` and `5`.

## Running it yourself

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# full reproduction with figures (about 7 minutes), from the package source directory:
source(system.file("scripts", "RealDataAnalysis_package.R", package = "covassistedGM"))
```
